title: How to connect permanent roofline lighting to Google Home and Alexa
body_markdown:
Voice commands only work if the app finishes talking to your lighting fixtures before it starts talking to Alexa or Google — skip that order and you get a skill that links but finds zero devices. Get the roofline lighting app synced first, then hand the connection to Alexa or Google Home, and you're saying "turn on porch lights" within about 15 minutes.


**TL;DR**

- Connect permanent lighting to Alexa by linking the manufacturer's skill first, then running Discover Devices — most setups take under 15 minutes in 2026.
- Google Home uses the same order: link the service under Works with Google, then let it scan for fixtures.
- 2.4GHz Wi-Fi is the most common failure point — most roofline lighting hubs won't pair on 5GHz-only networks.
- Sunset-triggered routines beat fixed-time schedules because daylight length changes month to month.
- CleanGutters Lighting installs and configures permanent roofline LED systems across South Jersey, Eastern PA, and Northern Delaware.


## Why this matters

A permanent roofline lighting system that only turns on from a wall switch is half a system. The point of running it through [CleanGutters Lighting](https://cleangutterslighting.com/) or any custom architectural lighting install is the control layer — schedules, voice, color changes for holidays without a ladder. If the smart home connection isn't set up correctly, homeowners end up manually flipping breakers for a system that was supposed to remove that chore entirely.

The process below applies to any Wi-Fi-based permanent roofline lighting system with a companion app — which covers the overwhelming majority of installs done in 2026. The exact app name varies by manufacturer, but the pairing sequence with Alexa and Google Home is nearly identical across brands.

## Before you start

- **Your home Wi-Fi name and password for the 2.4GHz band.** Most roofline lighting hubs pair on 2.4GHz only, not 5GHz — if your router broadcasts one combined network name for both bands, note it, because this is the single most common setup failure.
- **The lighting system's own app installed and already showing your fixtures as connected**, before you touch Alexa or Google Home. Linking a skill to a hub with zero paired zones just gives you an empty device list.
- **The Alexa or Google Home app installed and signed into the account you actually use every day** — not a secondary account, or you'll see the lights in one app and nothing in the other.

## Confirm your roofline lighting app is live

1. Open the manufacturer's lighting app and check that every zone (front roofline, garage line, accent) shows a connected or online status, not "pairing" or grayed out.
2. Turn one zone on and off manually from the app to confirm the hub is actually responding, not just showing cached status.
3. Note the exact account email or username you used to create the lighting app account — you'll need to enter it again during the skill link.

**Expected result:** every installed zone shows online in the app and responds to a manual on/off toggle within a couple seconds.

### Link the skill in the Alexa app

1. Open the Alexa app and tap **More** in the bottom navigation bar.
2. Tap **Skills & Games**, then search for your lighting manufacturer's name in the search bar.
3. Tap the skill, then tap **Enable to Use**.
4. On the account screen, tap **Link Account** and log in with the same email and password used in the lighting app.
5. Tap **Authorize** to grant Alexa permission to control your fixtures.
6. Return to the Alexa home screen, tap **Devices**, then **+**, then **Discover Devices**.

**Expected result:** each connected zone appears as a separate device in the Alexa app, named whatever you labeled it in the manufacturer's app.

### Add the service in Google Home

1. Open the Google Home app and tap **Devices**.
2. Tap the **+** icon, then select **Works with Google**.
3. Search for the lighting manufacturer's name and select it from the results.
4. Sign in with your lighting app credentials and tap **Allow** on the permissions screen.
5. Google Home scans automatically — give it 20 to 30 seconds before assuming it failed.

**Expected result:** your roofline lighting zones appear under Devices, grouped by whatever room or zone name you assigned in the manufacturer's app.


![Four-step diagram showing the order for connecting roofline lighting to a smart home app](https://gwvckixiegkllthleuyt.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/workspace-article-images-public/116e21c3-de4f-4ce1-b030-d041a73c5ad9/body-9cf5d2b3958e83411d526bb693daebbf.jpg)

*Linking the skill before confirming the lighting app is connected is the most common reason Discover Devices comes back empty.*


## Run color changes and schedules automatically

Once the fixtures show up as devices, you can skip manual toggling entirely by building a routine instead. This is the same connection you just made — you're just using it for automation instead of one-off voice commands.

**In Alexa:** go to **More**, then **Routines**, then **+** to create one. Set the trigger to **Sunset**, not a fixed clock time — daylight length shifts through the year, and a fixed 6:00 PM trigger looks wrong by December when it's dark at 4:45.

**In Google Home:** tap **Automations**, then **+**, then choose a trigger like **Sunset** or a specific time, and set the action to turn on the roofline lighting devices at a chosen color or brightness.

For holiday color changes — red and green for the season, orange for October — most manufacturer apps let you save a color preset by zone, then trigger that preset through the same routine instead of rebuilding it from scratch every year.



## Troubleshooting

- **Discover Devices finds nothing.** Confirm your phone and the lighting hub are on the same 2.4GHz network — a hub paired to a guest network or a 5GHz-only band won't show up no matter how many times you rescan.
- **The skill says "Account already linked" but no devices appear.** Unlink the skill completely, restart the lighting hub by unplugging it for 10 seconds, then relink from scratch.
- **Voice command turns on the wrong zone.** Rename the zones in the manufacturer's app first, then unlink and relink the skill — Alexa and Google Home both pull zone names from the source app, not the other way around.
- **Routine doesn't trigger at all.** Check that the routine's trigger device (the roofline lighting zone) still shows as online in the smart home app — a hub that dropped offline overnight silently breaks any routine depending on it.
- **Two people in the same house each see different devices.** This usually means two separate Alexa or Google accounts exist in the home instead of one shared account — consolidate to one before troubleshooting anything else.

## Customize your setup

Once voice and schedules work, most homeowners add per-zone brightness limits (dimmer for a bedroom-facing roofline run, full brightness for the street-facing front), and separate holiday presets saved under different names so switching for the Fourth of July doesn't require rebuilding the whole routine. If the roofline lighting itself isn't installed yet, or the current setup wasn't wired with zoning in mind, that's a job for the install, not the app.

## FAQ


**How do I connect permanent lighting to Alexa?**

Open the Alexa app, go to More, then Skills & Games, search for your lighting manufacturer, enable the skill, link your account, and run Discover Devices. Your zones appear under Alexa's Devices tab once linked, usually within a minute of tapping Discover.

**Does permanent roofline lighting work with Google Home?**

Yes, as long as the manufacturer offers a Google Home integration under Works with Google. The setup mirrors Alexa: link the account first, then let Google Home scan for devices.

**Why won't my lighting hub show up when I try to discover devices?**

The most common cause in 2026 is a Wi-Fi band mismatch — the hub is trying to pair on 2.4GHz while your phone or router pushed it onto 5GHz. Split your network's bands temporarily if your router combines them into one name.

**Can I schedule roofline lighting to change color for holidays automatically?**

Yes, most manufacturer apps let you save color presets by zone, then trigger those presets through an Alexa Routine or Google Home Automation on a set date or sunset trigger.

**Is a fixed time or sunset trigger better for outdoor lighting schedules?**

Sunset triggers hold up better year-round because daylight length changes by roughly 4-5 hours between summer and winter. A fixed 6:00 PM trigger looks off by two months into the season.

**Why does my roofline lighting show up in Alexa but not Google Home?**

Each platform requires a separate account link — enabling the Alexa skill does not automatically connect Google Home. Repeat the linking steps inside the Google Home app using the same lighting app credentials.

**Do I need a smart hub to connect roofline lighting to Alexa?**

Most permanent roofline LED systems ship with their own Wi-Fi hub that bridges to Alexa and Google Home through the manufacturer's app — you generally don't need a separate third-party hub.


## One last thing

The zone names you set during install are permanent from a voice-command standpoint — renaming "Front Roofline" to "Porch Lights" later means unlinking and relinking the skill, not just editing a label in Alexa. Get the zone names right in the manufacturer's app on day one, before either skill gets linked, and this whole setup only takes one pass in 2026 instead of two.
